How would you describe the investment backdrop during the 12 months ended July 31, 2026?

As a group, preferred stocks provided enough income to offset much, but not all, of a decline in market prices that was triggered by changing interest-rate expectations. During much of late 2025 and then again briefly in early spring 2026, preferred stocks were supported by market expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve would cut policy interest-rates. The prices of preferred stocks generally rise when interest rates fall and vice versa because their fixed dividends become more or less attractive relative to newly issued securities. Later in the period, however, preferred stock prices generally declined. Rising inflation worries — including those driven by tariffs and the oil-price shock from the Iran war — led markets to push out the timing of interest rate cuts, and by late in the period, to price in the possibility of interest rate hikes.

How did the fund perform?

Among the fund’s top-performing individual holdings were convertible preferred securities from Bank of America Corp. Their gains largely reflected the bank’s rising net interest income, resilient consumer credit and strong trading and investment-banking results. The convertible preferred shares of PG&E Corp., whose principal subsidiary, Pacific Gas and Electric Company, supplies electricity and natural gas across much of Northern and central California, also lifted performance.

Cash and short-term investments are not included.

Their advance was powered by powered by improving earnings and increased electricity demand. Elsewhere, the preferred shares of Telephone & Data Systems, Inc. also aided fund performance, bolstered primarily by the sale of wireless operations and selected spectrum to T-Mobile USA, Inc. and a separate spectrum sale to AT&T, Inc. Exposure to the convertible preferred shares of electric power company NextEra Energy, Inc. was another plus for performance because it was boosted by the dramatic growth in electricity consumption associated with artificial intelligence infrastructure.

In contrast, exposure to Strategy, Inc., which functions primarily as a Bitcoin treasury company, was the largest individual detractor. Its preferred share prices significantly declined along with the price of the cryptocurrency. Another detractor was FMC Corp., a U.S. agricultural sciences company whose shares lost value as the patent protection expired on its important insecticide technology, allowing lower-priced competitors to enter major Asian and Latin American markets. Holdings in the preferred stock of Whirlpool Corp. disappointed as the sluggish U.S. housing market muted demand for major household appliances. Holdings in insurance and annuity provider Brighthouse Financial, Inc. performed poorly primarily due to concerns that the company’s plan to go private would be less favorable to preferred stock investors than for its common stock shareholders.
